name: Making predictions with few examples or limited data
gist: Theoretical analysis of learning when data is scarce, including in-context learning, active selection of which data to gather, and efficient use of existing knowledge.
explain: A radiologist spends years learning to read X-rays before they can diagnose rare diseases accurately. They can learn from few examples because they already understand anatomy, physiology, and common pathologies, which provides a foundation. A new model trained from scratch, given only ten examples of a rare disease, has no such foundation and would need far more examples. Yet modern large language models seem to learn from a few examples in seconds — asking a model to classify text after showing just three examples of the desired classification often works, which suggests that large pretraining gives access to hidden knowledge about language and reasoning. This subtheme investigates: how can learning happen with very limited data — what mechanisms allow a model to adapt with so few examples — and what hidden knowledge enables this by providing a foundation the way a radiologist's years of study do?

The challenge is that pure statistical learning theory says you need roughly as many examples as you have weights to estimate. If a model has a million weights, you need about a million examples to confidently learn. But you often have far fewer examples than weights. Somehow, pretrained models that learned on large datasets transfer their knowledge to new tasks, or architectural biases built into networks exploit hidden structure in problems. In some cases, you can select which examples to learn from (active learning), focusing on the most informative examples rather than random ones. In other cases, you get to see examples one at a time and adapt after each one (online learning). Understanding how to learn from scarce data requires using what was known before (foundations from other tasks or domains), structure in the problem, or the ability to choose wisely which data to use.

Researchers study few-shot learning — learning from only a handful of examples — by analyzing when and why transfer learning works. They investigate in-context learning in large models, where the model reads instructions and examples in its input and adapts its behavior without updating weights. They analyze active learning strategies that select the most informative examples to learn from, reducing the total examples needed. They study meta-learning — learning how to learn — where a model trained on many tasks learns to adapt quickly to new tasks. They also examine data augmentation (creating new examples from old ones through transformations) and regularization techniques that encode assumptions about the problem structure. The goal is to extract the most learning from each example and use what was known before to fill gaps where data is scarce.

papers.title: Active Learning for Decision Trees with Provable Guarantees
papers.contribution: Achieves polylogarithmic label complexity in dataset size under stated assumptions, with label complexity lower bound showing algorithm dependence on error tolerance epsilon is close to optimal.

papers.title: Active Regression for Single-Index Models with Unknown Link Functions
papers.contribution: Closes remaining gaps in active ell-p regression theory for single-index models with unknown link functions.

papers.title: An evolutionary perspective on modes of learning in Transformers
papers.contribution: Stable environments favor IWL with sharp transitions; reliable cues favor ICL in volatile settings; task structure governs strategy transitions.

papers.title: DreamDojo: A Generalist Robot World Model from Large-Scale Human Videos
papers.contribution: Closes remaining gaps in active ell-p regression theory for single-index models with unknown link functions.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning Without Forgetting In-Context Learning: A Theoretical Analysis of Linear Attention Models
papers.contribution: Identifies conditions under which fine-tuning degrades in-context learning and demonstrates theoretically and empirically that selective parameter updates enable both objectives.

papers.title: In-Context Universal Approximation, Compositional Generalization, and Algorithm Emulation
papers.contribution: The work provides concrete mechanisms by which GPT-style models execute and assemble algorithms in context, supporting a principled view of prompts as programs and frozen Transformers as program interpreters.

papers.title: Is In-Context Learning Learning?
papers.contribution: The analysis shows that accuracy is insensitive to exemplar distribution and model variation in high-exemplar regimes, and ICL's ad-hoc encoding mechanism does not provide robust all-purpose generalization.

papers.title: On the "Induction Bias" in Sequence Models
papers.contribution: Transformers require substantially more training data than RNNs as state-space size and sequence length grow, learn length-specific solutions with negligible weight sharing, while RNNs exhibit effective amortized learning across lengths.

papers.title: Active Learning with Low-Rank Structure for Data Selection
papers.contribution: This perspective was further explored by Axiotis et.

papers.title: Asymptotic Theory of Iterated Empirical Risk Minimization, with Applications to Active Learning
papers.contribution: Removes oracle and sample-splitting assumptions in active learning, uncovering fundamental budget allocation tradeoff and double-descent driven purely by data selection.

papers.title: Causal-EPIG: Causally Aligned Active CATE Estimation
papers.contribution: Improves sample efficiency over standard baselines and shows context-dependent strategy preference contingent on base estimator and treatment-effect structure.

papers.title: High-dimensional Analysis of Synthetic Data Selection
papers.contribution: Covariance matching is optimal in some regimes; the theoretical insights for linear models carry over to deep neural networks, and covariance matching outperforms recent synthetic data selection approaches.

papers.title: How Can Mamba Learn In Context with Outliers and Generalize Provably?
papers.contribution: Demonstrates Mamba maintains accurate predictions even when outlier proportion exceeds Transformer thresholds, supported by empirical verification on binary classification.

papers.title: How Does the Pretraining Distribution Shape In-Context Learning? A Fundamental Trade-Off
papers.contribution: Reveals fundamental design trade-off: heavy-tailed distributions improve robust task selection but hurt generalization; frameworks informed by dependent sequence theory.

papers.title: Learning $U$-Statistics with Active Inference
papers.contribution: Demonstrates substantial gains in estimation efficiency over baselines while maintaining target coverage on real datasets.

papers.title: On the Difficulty of Learning a Meta-network for Training Data Selection
papers.contribution: Simple solution of increasing batch size plus feature engineering yields average gains of 5.49% over training without selection and 2.89% over strongest baseline across four benchmarks.

papers.title: Pretrain–Test Task Alignment Governs Generalization in In-Context Learning
papers.contribution: Identifies train-test task alignment as key ICL generalization determinant, revealing trade-off between specialization and generalization depending on task distribution alignment.

papers.title: STAND: Self-Aware Precondition Induction for Interactive Task Learning
papers.contribution: Beats XGBoost, decision trees, random forests, and version spaces at small-data precondition induction while maintaining high accuracy at estimating when performance improves on holdout examples.

papers.title: The Power of Power Law: Asymmetry Enables Compositional Reasoning
papers.contribution: Across compositional reasoning tasks, power-law distributions consistently outperform uniform, with theoretical analysis explaining improved loss landscape.

papers.title: Theory of Scaling Laws for In-Context Regression: Depth, Width, Context and Time
papers.contribution: Depth aids ICL only with limited context in isotropic/fixed settings, but significantly helps with changing covariances.

papers.title: Understanding In-Context Learning on Structured Manifolds: Bridging Attention to Kernel Methods
papers.contribution: When sufficient training tasks are observed, transformers achieve minimax regression rates for Hölder functions on manifolds, with complexity scaling exponentially with prompt length by intrinsic manifold dimension.

papers.title: Understanding the Role of Training Data in Test-Time Scaling
papers.contribution: Characterizes task hardness via the smallest eigenvalue of feature covariance; shows training on diverse, relevant, and hard tasks results in best test-time scaling performance.

papers.title: Universal Approximation with Softmax Attention
papers.contribution: Establishes that softmax-attention-only layers are capable of approximating gradient descent in-context and subsume many known universal approximators.

papers.title: What Does Preference Learning Recover from Pairwise Comparison Data?
papers.contribution: Offers data-centric foundation for understanding preference learning, identifying margin and connectivity as critical factors for learnability.

papers.title: When More Experts Hurt: Underfitting in Multi-Expert Learning to Defer
papers.contribution: Resolves multi-expert underfitting; proves statistical consistency and ability to recover class probabilities and expert accuracies; validated on diverse settings including real-world expert scenarios.

papers.title: Why Ask One When You Can Ask $k$? Learning-to-Defer to the Top-$k$ Experts
papers.contribution: Top-k and Top-k(x) deliver superior accuracy-cost trade-offs across one-stage and two-stage regimes compared to top-1 deferral.
